findings.explanation: UPS's published Tracking API specification lists the production host as https://onlinetools.ups.com/api (CIE: wwwcie.ups.com), with OAuth tokens from onlinetools.ups.com/security/v1/oauth/token. api.ups.com is not the documented host. The same wrong host appears in app, implementation and detailedImplementation (including the OAuth token URL).
findings.suggested_fix: Use https://onlinetools.ups.com/api/track/v1/details/{inquiryNumber} with an OAuth token from https://onlinetools.ups.com/security/v1/oauth/token everywhere. Also drop the 'UPS Tracking API v3' label, since the resource is v1.

findings.explanation: USPS retired the Web Tools API platform, including Track/Confirm, on 25 January 2026. A reader building a USPS collector from this text would target a shut-down service. The prerequisites and the USPS Web Tools reference repeat the same dependency.
findings.quote: USPS Web Tools Track/Confirm API v1.1 ASCII payloads mirrored into Splunk
findings.suggested_fix: Replace it with the USPS APIs platform: Tracking 3.2 at https://apis.usps.com (OAuth 2.0, optionally Subscriptions - Tracking 3.2 webhooks), and update the reference link.

findings.explanation: This mixes FedEx's legacy SOAP Web Services (being retired in favour of REST APIs on developer.fedex.com) with OAuth REST. The webhook signature header 'x-fedex-signature', UPS 'x-ups-token' and DHL 'x-dhl-signature' look guessed. The claim that UPS 'MV' activity codes mean signature-required reroutes is also doubtful.
findings.quote: FedEx Track Notification payloads (SOAP-over-HTTP XML envelopes referencing Track Web Services scan-event enumerations OD/DL/DE alongside OAuth client_credentials tokens
findings.suggested_fix: Check the FedEx Advanced Integrated Visibility webhook documentation (payload format and signature header), the UPS Track Alert docs, and DHL's webhook guide. Use only documented header names and status-code meanings, and describe FedEx ingestion as REST/JSON.

findings.explanation: The project44 path and version are not confirmed by the reference, which links only the project44 home page. Current project44 visibility APIs are versioned differently.
findings.quote: TMS normalization lanes poll project44 Movement GET /api/v3/tracking/shipments/{id}
findings.suggested_fix: Check against project44's developer documentation and correct the path. Link the specific API reference page.

findings.explanation: Exchange, Microsoft 365, SNMP and the 'snmp_ups' power-supply model have nothing to do with parcel tracking. 'snmp_ups' was probably matched on the carrier name UPS. PagerDuty and ServiceNow are alert destinations, not data sources.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep db_connect (and salesforce only if SFCC is meant to be a first-class source), and drop the rest.

findings.explanation: The SPL has no eventstats. on_time_pct comes from a second stats. Step 2 also says weekend subtraction uses 'heuristic placeholders', and Step 4 says paging needs a sustained four-hour window, which the SPL does not implement.
findings.quote: eventstats aggregates on_time_pct slices grouped carrier_norm × svc_bucket × hourly buckets feeding threshold filters
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the actual pipeline stages, and mark the four-hour persistence check as a separate summary-index step with its own search.

findings.explanation: The sentence is ungrammatical ('what record shows'). 'Lane by lane' is logistics jargon. The reference to sibling UCs ('dock receipts or invoice bundles studied elsewhere') means nothing to a lay reader, and the explanation never says that late carriers and areas are flagged.
findings.quote: We line up what people were told about when a box would arrive with what record shows happened at the door—street by street and lane by lane—without mixing that picture with dock receipts or invoice bundles studied elsewhere.
findings.suggested_fix: For example: 'We compare the delivery date customers were promised with when each parcel actually arrived, by carrier, service and area, and flag the carriers and neighbourhoods where too many parcels arrive late or need repeat delivery attempts.'

findings.explanation: The status says verified, but the reviewer is an agent, and the UC depends on a retired USPS API and a wrong UPS host, so no SME verification is evident.
findings.suggested_fix: Set the status to draft or community until a logistics SME validates the feeds.

findings.explanation: The project44, DHL, MetaPack and Pitney Bowes entries link home pages rather than the API reference or report named in the title.
findings.suggested_fix: Link the specific project44 and DHL API reference pages, or drop the entries.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `business_days_taken` and `sla_met` are evaluated per event, before any correlation. Promised dates come from OMS extracts and actual delivery times from carrier scans, which are different events, so almost no single event has both. sla_met evaluates to 0 (isnull branches) for nearly every row. The promise and the delivery must first be joined per tracking_number (for example `stats latest(promised_delivery_at) latest(actual_delivery_at) by tracking_number`) and SLA computed afterwards. Grouping the first stats by dest_zip also splits OMS rows (with zip) from scan rows (often without) for the same parcel.
`sort tracking_number scan_ts` without a count truncates to 10,000 results, so 30 days of multi-carrier scans are cut off before streamstats and stats run. Use `sort 0 tracking_number scan_ts`.

`index=business earliest=-30d@d` has no sourcetype filter and no `where tracking_number!=""`, so every CRM, HR and finance event in the index becomes a 'parcel' with tracking_number "", which drags on_time_pct down. Restrict to the carrier, TMS and OMS sourcetypes named in detailedImplementation Step 2.

`holiday_flag=if(match(dest_zip,"^430|^441|^972|^381"),1,0)` hard-codes four zip prefixes as a 'holiday' flag and uses it to forgive weather/force-majeure exceptions. `failed_first_attempt_rate=round(avg_failed_attempts*12,2)` applies an unexplained ×12 multiplier. Neither is defensible. Use a lookup of disruption windows by zip prefix and date, and compute first-attempt failure as parcels with nh_attempts>=1 divided by parcels.

The final grouping by carrier × service × dest_zip × hour gives cells of one or two parcels with no minimum-volume guard, so `on_time_pct < 95` fires on a single late parcel. revenue_at_risk also assigns free_shipping_credit_value to parcels that were on time (`business_days_taken<=1 OR sla_met=1`), which inverts the intent.

summary: The pitfalls list is rich and real (scan-order inversion, SmartPost handoffs, locker deliveries, timezone skew), but the build guidance has wrong facts. The UPS host is wrong, USPS Web Tools has been retired, and the FedEx SOAP and REST paths are mixed up. The SPL computes SLA per event before joining OMS promises to carrier deliveries, sorts with a 10,000-row cap, scans the whole business index, and uses magic constants (hard-coded 'holiday' zip prefixes, ×12 failed-attempt rate).
